claims.text: High configurational entropy in HEAs induces lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions slow the diffusion of oxide-forming elements.
Slower diffusion of oxide-forming elements enables formation of a coherent, adherent, and self-healing protective oxide layer.
The proposed HEA contains multiple principal elements, including Cr or Al, in near-equiatomic proportions.
The proposed initial microstructure is disordered and homogenized.
Lattice distortions and a uniform grain-boundary structure confine diffusion of key elements in the HEA.
Confinement of key-element diffusion stabilizes the developing oxide scale.
Reduced diffusion of Cr and Al promotes a slow-growing, uniform, and adherent oxide layer.
The resulting self-limiting oxide scale impedes further oxidation.
The self-limiting scale maintains a protective barrier at high temperatures.
Under identical oxidation conditions, HEAs will form thinner oxide scales than conventional lower-entropy alloys.
Under identical oxidation conditions, HEA oxide scales will be more uniform and better adhered than those on conventional alloys.
HEAs will exhibit a coherent substrate–oxide interface.
Oxide-growth kinetics will be suppressed in HEAs relative to conventional alloys.
Conventional lower-entropy alloys with similar oxide-forming elements typically form thicker and less uniform oxide scales with faster oxidation kinetics.
The proposed mechanism applies to HEAs containing sufficient concentrations of oxide-forming elements under controlled high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Severe thermal cycling, aggressive environmental species, and extreme composition changes may alter the oxidation dynamics and fall outside the hypothesis boundary.
